body:
Wildcard (`"*"`) topic discovery runs once per `PubSubSource.events()` call (process start). Discovery failures now retry 3x with backoff (see `_discover_with_retry` in `src/sf2loki/sources/pubsub_source.py`), but a channel *created after startup* (e.g. Salesforce enables a new `*EventStream` entity, or an admin turns on more Event Monitoring streams) is not picked up until the process restarts.

**Impact:** new event types silently unmonitored between deploys.

**Resolution steps:**
1. Add a background task in `PubSubSource.events()` that re-runs `_discover_with_retry()` on an interval (suggest 1h, configurable).
2. Diff against the live topic set.
3. For additions, spawn a new `_run_topic` task and increment the sentinel bookkeeping accordingly — the drain loop must account for late-spawned producers (this bookkeeping is why it was deferred as non-minimal).
4. Removals can be ignored (a deleted channel's stream just ends).
5. Keep the include/exclude glob filter in mind, and note the overlap guard currently runs at startup in `app.py` against `resolve_topics()` — late-added topics bypass it and need a runtime check or documented exemption (see the companion overlap-guard issue).

body:
The startup overlap guard (`check_overlap` in `src/sf2loki/sources/overlap.py`, wired in `App.build`) only sees identifiers configured at startup. ELF wildcard discovery already skips categories owned by other sources at poll time (`EventLogFileSource` `exclude_categories`), but wildcard-discovered **Pub/Sub topics** get no equivalent runtime check — `topics: ["*"]` can double-ingest a category owned by `eventlog_objects`/`eventlogfile`.

**Impact:** silent double-ingestion (duplicate log volume + cost) in wildcard-on-both-sides configs. A docs caveat now exists in `docs/configuring-sources.md` §1, but the guard should enforce it.

**Resolution steps:**
1. Compute the owned-category set (stored objects + explicit ELF types) in `App.build` and pass it to `PubSubSource`.
2. At topic-discovery time in the pubsub source, filter discovered topics via `category_of_pubsub` against that set (mirror `EventLogFileSource`'s exclusion), logging each skip at INFO.
3. Respect `sources.allow_overlap` (pass an empty set, as `App.build` already does for ELF).
4. Update the caveat in `docs/configuring-sources.md` §1 once enforced.

body:
The pipeline queue is bounded by entry count only: `queue_maxsize=10_000` hardcoded in `Pipeline.__init__` (`src/sf2loki/app.py`), plus a 1000-entry queue inside `PubSubSource`. Entries can carry up to `max_line_bytes` (256 KiB) each, so a prolonged Loki outage with fat ELF rows can theoretically buffer ~2.6 GB before backpressure engages. Typical rows are 1–2 KB so the common case is fine, but the container has no memory guarantee matching the worst case.

**Resolution steps (either/both):**
1. Track approximate bytes alongside entry count in the pipeline queue (an `asyncio.Condition`-guarded byte budget; the batch builder in `_consume` already computes `approx_bytes` per entry — reuse that accounting) and block producers on either limit.
2. Or minimally: expose `queue_maxsize` in config (e.g. `sink.loki.batch.queue_maxsize`), document the worst-case memory formula (`queue_maxsize x max_line_bytes`) in the config reference, and regen artifacts (`just gen-config`).

body:
`/readyz` is set once at startup (after the new fail-fast auth probe) and only un-sets on shutdown/leadership loss. Degraded modes keep the healthcheck green: all Pub/Sub topics stuck in reconnect loops, the sink retrying forever against a down/misauthed Loki, Salesforce auth broken post-startup. (The worst case — consumer-task death — now crashes the process, and permanent drops are loudly logged/counted, but slow degradation is still invisible to orchestrators.)

**Resolution steps:**
1. Add a per-topic `pubsub_stream_up`-style gauge (set 1 on healthy connection — the "healthy" signal from the backoff-reset logic in `_run_topic` is the natural hook — 0 on error/reconnect).
2. Track last-successful-push and last-commit timestamps in the pipeline; expose as gauges.
3. Mark `/readyz` degraded (or add a `/healthz` detail payload) when the sink has been retrying beyond N minutes or all streams are down; make thresholds configurable.
4. Document a recommended staleness alert (e.g. on `sf2loki_last_replay_commit_timestamp_seconds` age and `sf2loki_watermark_timestamp_seconds` age) in the Grafana dashboard docs, and consider adding the panels to `deploy/grafana/gen_dashboard.py`.

`EventLogObjectsSource.events()` sleeps on the FIRST configured object's `poll_interval` for all objects (self-acknowledged in a code comment in `src/sf2loki/sources/eventlog_objects_source.py`), while `docs/config-reference.md` presents `poll_interval` as per-object. Two objects configured at `5m`/`1h` both poll at whichever interval is listed first — extra API calls or staleness depending on order.

**Resolution steps:**
1. Either run one polling task per object (each with its own interval and jitter, feeding the same queue/generator — mind the checkpoint-carry semantics per object, which are already keyed per object), or
2. Compute per-object next-due timestamps in the single loop and sleep until the earliest.
3. Add tests for two objects with different intervals; update the code comment.
4. Alternatively (minimal): make `poll_interval` a source-level (not per-object) setting in config and regen artifacts — but that's a config-surface break, so prefer 1/2.

The ELF source counts failures via `sf2loki_eventlogfile_download_errors{reason}`; throttles are counted via `sf2loki_salesforce_api_throttled{api}`; generic ELO poll errors are invisible.

body:
`extract_timestamp` (`src/sf2loki/shaping.py`) falls back to `datetime.now(UTC)` when an event/row timestamp column is missing or unparseable. Replayed rows (at-least-once redelivery after a crash or an EARLIEST replay fallback) then get FRESH timestamps, defeating the "Loki drops byte-identical duplicates" dedup assumption for exactly those rows — they ingest as duplicates.

**Impact:** duplicate log lines for events with broken timestamps whenever a replay occurs; low frequency but silent.

**Resolution steps:**
1. Prefer a stable per-record fallback before ingest-time: for ELF rows, the file's `CreatedDate` (available in `EventLogFileMeta` at the call site); for Pub/Sub payloads, any `CreatedDate`/`EventDate`/`commitTimestamp` sibling field already probed by `_event_timestamp`.
2. Count fallback usage via a metric (e.g. reuse/extend `sf2loki_decode_errors` with a `reason="timestamp_fallback"` or a dedicated counter) so operators can see it happening.
3. Note the Loki out-of-order window (~1h per stream on Grafana Cloud): a stable-but-old fallback timestamp can be rejected as too old on replay — the 400-split path now isolates those, but consider clamping the fallback to `now - safety_margin` when the stable candidate is older than the OOO window. NOTE: This out-of-order loki concern is no more only the oldest timestamp matters (1w)

body:
Three small nags from the full operational audit, none urgent, batched here so they aren't lost:

**1. ELF carried-id window overflow churn.** `_MAX_CARRIED_IDS = 200` in `src/sf2loki/sources/eventlogfile_source.py`: if more than 200 files share one CreatedDate for one event type (bulk backfill / sandbox refresh), the id window can't cover them all and uncovered files are re-downloaded and re-emitted every cycle (duplicates + API burn, not loss — at-least-once holds). Fix: carry ids only for `created_date == watermark` and size the window dynamically, or log a WARNING when the cap truncates.

**2. Local-clock dependence in settle/abandon gates.** First-run `default_since`, the settle window, and `download_max_age` compare local `now` to Salesforce `CreatedDate`; minutes of clock skew shift settle/abandon behavior. Post-first-cycle watermarks are SF-clock-sourced (safe). Fix: derive "now" from a Salesforce response timestamp (e.g. the `Date` header or the max CreatedDate seen) where cheap, or document an NTP requirement.

**3. AvroCodec single global fetch lock.** `src/sf2loki/salesforce/avro_codec.py` serializes ALL schema fetches behind one lock — the first decode of schema B blocks behind a slow fetch of schema A. Cosmetic at current schema counts; per-schema-id locks would fix it if wildcard subscriptions grow.

body:
## Motivation
`--check` validates config/wiring offline, but the painful first-run failures are all *live*: wrong Connected/External Client App scopes, the execution user missing "View Event Log Files"/"View Real-Time Event Monitoring Data", no Event Monitoring entitlement (wildcards silently yield ~6 free types), an unreachable Pub/Sub channel, a Loki token without `logs:write`, or a state dir the container uid can't write. Today each of these surfaces one at a time, at runtime, as an error the operator has to interpret.

## Proposal
A `sf2loki doctor --config ...` subcommand that runs a sequenced, read-only-except-one-test-write diagnostic and prints a PASS/WARN/FAIL table:

1. Config load + secrets resolution (reuse `--check`).
2. Token mint (reports flow used, instance_url, org id; on failure prints the exact SF error body and likely cause — e.g. client_credentials off-My-Domain, un-preauthorized JWT user).
3. Permissions probe: `GET /services/data/vXX/sobjects/EventLogFile/describe` (View Event Log Files), query `LoginHistory LIMIT 1` if configured, Pub/Sub `GetTopic` on each resolved topic (catches missing RTEM entitlement/channel per topic).
4. Entitlement report: SOQL `SELECT EventType, Interval FROM EventLogFile GROUP BY EventType, Interval` (approximation via recent rows) → prints which event types actually exist in the org vs configured; WARN when a configured explicit type has produced no files.
5. Loki write test: push one line to a `source="sf2loki-doctor"` stream, report status/latency; on 401/403 print the tenant-id-vs-token guidance already in the README.
6. State dir: create/lock/fsync a probe file as the current uid; print the chmod/chown hint on failure.
7. Org limits snapshot (`/limits`): daily API calls remaining, warn if the configured poll cadence would consume a notable fraction.

## Implementation sketch
- New `doctor` subcommand in `src/sf2loki/cli.py`, orchestration module `src/sf2loki/doctor.py`; reuse `TokenProvider`, `SoqlClient`, `EventLogFileClient`, `PubSubClient.get_topic` (may need a thin `GetTopic` RPC wrapper — the stub already exists in the generated code), `LokiSink`.
- Each check = small async callable returning `(name, status, detail)`; run sequentially (auth first, dependents skip when auth fails); `--json` output flag for CI.
- Exit code 0 (all pass/warn) / 1 (any fail).
- Tests: unit-test each check against respx/fake gRPC fixtures, one integration test of the table rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
- A fresh user with a misconfigured app gets a single command that pinpoints scope, permission, entitlement, Loki, and state-dir problems with actionable messages.
- Documented in the README quickstart as step "verify".

body:
## Motivation
New adopters almost always want history: "load the last 30 days of Event Monitoring into Loki so I can evaluate dashboards today". The service's steady-state design deliberately starts from `lookback` (default 24h) and Loki rejects entries older than the per-stream out-of-order window (~1h behind the newest) — so simply cranking `lookback` up both floods the first cycle and gets rows rejected once newer data lands in a stream.

## Proposal
`sf2loki backfill --config ... --since 2026-06-01 [--until ...] [--event-types Login,API]` — a one-shot (non-daemon) run that:
1. Lists ELF records in the window (both intervals; prefer Daily for completeness per Salesforce docs), newest-last, and streams them through the existing shaping/sink path.
2. Solves the OOO problem explicitly — pick one, make it a flag:
   - `--label-suffix backfill` (default): adds a `backfill="true"` label so backfilled streams are distinct from live streams and never collide with the live head (documented cardinality cost: 2x streams during evaluation).
   - `--ingest-timestamps`: uses ingest-time timestamps with the true event time preserved in structured metadata (keeps stream count flat; loses native time placement).
3. Orders pushes oldest→newest per stream so within-backfill OOO never triggers.
4. Uses a separate checkpoint namespace (`backfill:<type>`) so it can resume if interrupted and never perturbs the live service's watermarks; safe to run while the daemon is running.
5. Respects the API budget: bounded download concurrency + the existing throttle handling; prints a progress summary (files, rows, bytes, API calls used).

## Implementation sketch
- New `backfill` subcommand in `cli.py`; reuse `EventLogFileClient` (streaming download already lands O(row)), `route_fields`/`promote_labels`, `LokiSink`, `FileCheckpointStore` with the `backfill:` prefix.
- The label-suffix mode is a dict merge before push; the ingest-timestamp mode passes `fallback=now` unconditionally and moves the parsed event time into structured metadata key `event_time`.
- Retention guard: warn when `--since` is older than the org's ELF retention (1 day free / 30 days with the add-on) and than Loki's `reject_old_samples_max_age` (168h default) in label-suffix mode.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user can load 30 days of history into distinct, queryable streams with one command, resumable, without touching the live daemon's checkpoints or exceeding API limits.

body:
## Motivation
The sink speaks only the Loki push API. Metrics already egress via OTLP. An OTLP logs option would let sf2loki feed any OpenTelemetry collector (Alloy, otel-collector) or the Grafana Cloud OTLP endpoint directly — unlocking processor pipelines (transform, tail sampling, routing) and non-Loki backends without a shipper in between. It also consolidates auth: one OTLP credential for logs + metrics.

## Proposal
`sink.type: loki | otlp` (default `loki`, no behavior change). The OTLP variant maps the existing `LogEntry` model onto OTLP `LogRecord`s:
- labels → resource attributes (they're stream identity; `service.name=sf2loki`, plus `source`, `event_type`, operator statics)
- structured metadata + the JSON line fields → log attributes / body
- event timestamp → `time_unix_nano`; ingest time → `observed_time_unix_nano`

## Implementation sketch
- New `src/sf2loki/sinks/otlp/` implementing the same `Sink` protocol (`push(batch)`, `aclose`) so the pipeline (batching, retry classification, checkpoint-after-push, split-on-4xx semantics) is reused unchanged. Map HTTP statuses to the existing `RetryableSinkError`/`PermanentSinkError` taxonomy (OTLP partial-success responses count successes and log rejected counts).
- Prefer hand-rolled protobuf via the already-vendored OTLP proto from the metrics exporter dependency, or use `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http`'s `LogExporter` — evaluate which preserves the batch-level retry semantics cleanly (the SDK exporter hides status codes; hand-rolling the POST like the Loki sink does is probably cleaner and keeps tenacity/Retry-After handling identical).
- Config: `sink.otlp.{endpoint, headers, auth basic/bearer, compression}` mirroring `telemetry.*`; forbid configuring both sinks (or explicitly support fan-out later — out of scope here).
- Docs: which Grafana Cloud endpoint/creds to use; note that Loki-derived features (structured metadata behavior, OOO windows) differ behind the OTLP gateway.

## Acceptance criteria
- `sink.type: otlp` ships the same events to an OTLP endpoint with identical at-least-once checkpoint semantics and the full existing retry/drop observability (`loki_push`/`loki_entries_dropped` renamed or aliased appropriately).

body:
## Motivation
`EventLogFileSource` processes event types strictly sequentially within a cycle, and files sequentially within a type. A wildcard org with the Event Monitoring add-on has ~70 types; a cycle is 70 SOQL listings plus every download, one at a time. With hourly files and busy orgs, cycle time can approach or exceed the poll interval, adding hours of avoidable ingest latency (on top of Salesforce's inherent 3–6h ELF delay).

## Proposal
Process event types concurrently under a semaphore (suggest `sources.eventlogfile.concurrency`, default 4), keeping per-type ordering strictly sequential (the checkpoint-carry invariants are per type, so types are independent by construction).

## Implementation sketch
- In `_run_cycle` (or equivalent), wrap `_process_event_type` calls in tasks gated by `asyncio.Semaphore(cfg.concurrency)`; gather with the existing per-cycle error containment so one type's failure never affects others (already true sequentially — keep it true concurrently).
- The pipeline queue is shared and thread-safe (asyncio single loop) — entries from different types interleave, which is fine because checkpoint keys are per type and `_commit` takes the last token per key. Verify with a test that interleaved types commit independently correct checkpoints.
- Respect the throttle path: on `EventLogFileThrottledError`, cancel/skip the remaining types for the cycle (mirrors today's abort-rest-of-cycle) — a shared `throttled` event checked before each new task starts.
- Keep download streaming memory bounds in mind: concurrency multiplies peak spool usage; document `concurrency x spool_max` and default conservatively.
- Metrics: existing per-type counters already labelled; add cycle duration gauge (`sf2loki_eventlogfile_cycle_seconds`) to make the win visible.

## Acceptance criteria
- A 70-type wildcard cycle completes ~concurrency-times faster on listing/download-bound orgs, with unchanged checkpoint correctness (tests for interleaved commits + throttle abort) and documented memory bounds.

body:
## Motivation
Salesforce Event Monitoring volume is spiky and partly outside the operator's control (an API storm or a login wave can 10x volume overnight), and Loki-based platforms bill on ingested bytes. There is currently no way to bound what sf2loki will send: a runaway event type can blow through a log budget before anyone notices. Commercial Salesforce log integrations treat volume controls as a first-class feature; an OSS shipper needs them even more.

## Proposal
Three independent, per-config controls (all off by default):
1. **Per-type sampling**: `sources.eventlogfile.event_types[].sample: 0.25` (and an equivalent for pubsub topics / eventlog_objects) — keep a deterministic fraction of rows. Deterministic by hash of a stable row key (e.g. REQUEST_ID or the raw line), NOT random, so replays sample identically and Loki dedup still works.
2. **Rate cap**: `sink.loki.max_lines_per_second` / `max_bytes_per_second` — token-bucket delay applied at the pipeline (backpressure, not drop; the structural backpressure chain to flow control/polling already exists and does the right thing upstream).
3. **Daily byte budget**: `sink.loki.daily_byte_budget` — when the UTC-day pushed-bytes counter crosses the budget, either `pause` (default: stop pushing, hold checkpoints, resume next day — data delayed, not lost, up to ELF retention) or `drop` (count via `loki_entries_dropped{reason="budget"}`). Loud WARNING at 80%, ERROR at 100%.

## Implementation sketch
- Sampling: a `should_keep(row_key, rate)` helper in `shaping.py` (`hash(key) % 10_000 < rate*10_000`); applied in each source before yielding; counted via a new `sf2loki_entries_sampled_out{source,event_type}` counter (metrics.py addition).
- Rate cap: token bucket in `Pipeline._flush`/`_consume` before push; reuse `loki_bytes_pushed` accounting.
- Budget: UTC-day-keyed accumulator persisted in the state store (so restarts don't reset it), checked in `_flush`; `pause` mode holds like a retryable sink error (the existing readiness degradation will surface long pauses — document that interaction and consider a distinct reason string).
- Docs: a "controlling cost" section with the interplay between sampling (lossy, cheap) and budget-pause (lossless, delayed).

## Acceptance criteria
- An operator can cap worst-case daily spend with one config line, see sampling/drop/pause decisions in metrics and logs, and replay-safety (deterministic sampling) is test-proven.

body:
## Motivation
RTEM and EventLogFile rows carry personal data by design: source IPs, usernames, session ids, URIs with query strings, sometimes SOQL text containing customer data. Many orgs cannot ship these to a third-party log platform unredacted (GDPR/works-council constraints are the common blocker for exactly this class of tool). Today the only knobs are structured-metadata routing and label promotion — nothing removes or masks values.

## Proposal
Declarative per-source transform rules, applied after CSV/Avro decode and before shaping:
```yaml
sources:
  eventlogfile:
    transforms:
      - fields: [SOURCE_IP, CLIENT_IP]
        action: hash          # sha256 with a configurable per-deployment salt -> stable pseudonym
      - fields: [USER_NAME]
        action: mask          # keep domain, mask local part: "***@example.com"
      - fields: [SOQL_TEXT, REQUEST_BODY]
        action: drop_field
      - match: {EVENT_TYPE: "Sites"}
        action: drop_row
```
Actions: `drop_field`, `drop_row` (with `match` equality/glob on field values), `hash` (salted SHA-256, so correlation within a deployment still works), `mask` (format-aware for emails/IPs: `/24` truncation option), `regex_replace` (pattern + replacement, for URI query strings).

## Implementation sketch
- New `src/sf2loki/transforms.py` with a compiled rule pipeline built at config load (config models validate field names and regexes fail-fast; `extra="forbid"` style errors); each source calls `apply_transforms(payload)` at its decode boundary (ELF row dict, pubsub decoded payload, ELO record).
- Keep it deterministic and cheap: precompiled regexes, no per-row allocation beyond the mutated dict; benchmark against the streaming CSV path.
- Metric: `sf2loki_rows_filtered{source,rule}` for drop_row; field-level actions are silent by design (they'd be per-row-noise).
- IMPORTANT interaction: transforms run BEFORE `route_fields`, `promote_labels`, and `extract_timestamp` — document that redacting the timestamp column triggers the timestamp-fallback path, and forbid redacting reserved label fields at config load.
- Docs: a worked GDPR-ish example (hash IPs, mask usernames, drop SOQL text).

## Acceptance criteria
- An operator can express "never send raw IPs or usernames" in config, verified by tests including replay determinism (hash stability) and a config-validation failure for redacting reserved fields.

## Motivation
The dashboard now exposes every data-loss and degradation signal, but nothing alerts on them — operators must reverse-engineer thresholds from the metric docs. The failure modes that matter are known precisely (we built the metrics for them); shipping opinionated alert rules turns "observable" into "operated".

## Proposal
A generated, provisionable alert-rule bundle in `deploy/grafana/` (same generator-script pattern as the dashboard) covering:
- **Data loss (page)**: `rate(sf2loki_loki_entries_dropped_total[5m]) > 0`; `increase(sf2loki_pubsub_replay_fallbacks_total[1h]) > 0` (a fallback means a possible gap).
- **Stalled ingestion (page)**: `time() - sf2loki_last_push_success_timestamp_seconds > 900` while `sf2loki_queue_depth > 0`; `min by (topic) (sf2loki_pubsub_stream_up) == 0 for 15m`; watermark age: `time() - sf2loki_watermark_timestamp_seconds > 4x poll interval` (templated threshold).
- **Degradation (warn)**: `rate(sf2loki_soql_poll_errors_total[15m]) > 0`; `increase(sf2loki_pubsub_stream_stalls_total[1h]) > 0`; `rate(sf2loki_salesforce_api_throttled_total[15m]) > 0`; `sf2loki_salesforce_limit_remaining{limit_name="DailyApiRequests"} / sf2loki_salesforce_limit_max < 0.1`.
- **Hygiene (info)**: `rate(sf2loki_timestamp_fallbacks_total[1h]) > 0`; `rate(sf2loki_lines_truncated_total[1h]) > 0`.

## Implementation sketch
- `deploy/grafana/gen_alerts.py` emitting Grafana provisioning YAML (alert rule groups, folder `sf2loki`, datasource UID templated the same way the dashboard does it) + the committed generated file; document import via provisioning or `gcx`/HTTP API.
- Keep thresholds as variables at the top of the generator with rationale comments; label routing left to the operator (`severity` labels only).
- Also add an ingest-latency **histogram** (`sf2loki_ingest_lag` is a last-value gauge today; a histogram enables p95 alerting) — one metrics.py instrument + one call-site change in `Pipeline._produce`, and a dashboard panel swap.
- README ops section: table of shipped alerts with what each means and the first response step (this maps 1:1 to the failure modes documented in the audit).

## Acceptance criteria
- `docker compose` users can provision the alert pack with one documented step; each alert has a runbook-style description; drift gate covers the generated file like the dashboard.

body:
## Motivation
The single-replica constraint is documented and enforced per-host (state-file flock), but a host failure means ingestion stops until someone intervenes. The `Coordinator` seam (`src/sf2loki/coordinate/base.py`, DESIGN.md §13) was designed exactly for active-passive pairs — only the `NoopCoordinator` exists. Pub/Sub replay ids + ELF watermarks make failover naturally lossless (the standby resumes from committed checkpoints), so this is high-value, bounded work.

## Proposal
One (maybe two) real coordinator backends behind config `coordinate.type`:
1. **Kubernetes Lease** (`coordination.k8s.io/v1`) — the natural fit for k8s deployments; leader renews a Lease, standby watches and takes over on expiry.
2. **File lease on shared storage** (NFS/EFS) — for the docker-compose/VM crowd: lease file with holder-id + expiry, atomic renew via the existing tmp+rename pattern, takeover after expiry + grace. (Document the caveats of NFS locking honestly; the lease-expiry model avoids flock-over-NFS entirely.)

## Implementation sketch
- The seam already gates the pipeline on leadership (`on_acquire`/`on_lose` — verify exact shape in `coordinate/base.py` and `App.run`). Implement: acquire → run pipeline; lose → stop sources, flush, release the state-store flock, go standby; re-acquire → full source restart from checkpoints.
- Split-brain safety: the state store's flock already protects same-host; for shared-storage state, the lease holder-id must be written into the state dir and verified on every checkpoint flush (fencing token) — reject writes when the token doesn't match the current lease.
- `/readyz` on the standby returns 503 "standby" (orchestrators route/alert accordingly); a `sf2loki_leader` gauge (0/1).
- k8s backend uses `kubernetes_asyncio` as an optional extra (`pip install sf2loki[k8s]`) to keep the base image lean.
- Tests: lease takeover with a fake clock; fencing rejection when a stale leader tries to commit; the existing at-least-once invariants under a mid-batch failover (duplicates fine, loss not).

## Acceptance criteria
- Two replicas with `coordinate.type: k8s_lease` (or file lease + shared state dir) fail over automatically within the lease TTL, resume from checkpoints, never double-ingest for longer than one lease TTL, and never lose acknowledged data.

comments.body: Scope decision (maintainer): this issue ships the **file lease** backend only — it covers docker-compose/VM active-passive with zero new dependencies. The Kubernetes Lease backend is split out to #36.

body:
## Motivation
The file checkpoint store requires a persistent volume — awkward on ECS Fargate, Cloud Run, and other stateless-container platforms where a bind mount/EFS is the single biggest deployment friction. Checkpoints are tiny (one small JSON doc) and written at most once per batch flush, so object storage is a natural fit.

## Proposal
`state.type: file | s3 | gcs` (file remains default). S3/GCS store the same JSON document at a configured key, with optimistic concurrency to prevent split-brain clobbering:
- S3: conditional PUT (`If-Match` on ETag; S3 now supports conditional writes) or a versioned key + generation check.
- GCS: `ifGenerationMatch` preconditions (native compare-and-swap).

## Implementation sketch
- The `CheckpointStore` protocol is already minimal (`load`/`commit`). Implement `S3CheckpointStore`/`GcsCheckpointStore` in `src/sf2loki/state/`, caching the doc in memory like the file store and writing the whole doc per commit (batched: the pipeline already coalesces to last-token-per-key per flush, so write rate = flush rate, well within object-store rate limits; consider debouncing to ≥1s between PUTs).
- Durability semantics: commit must not return until the PUT is acknowledged (same contract the fsync gives the file store). On precondition failure → another writer exists → raise the same fail-fast error the flock gives locally (and this becomes the fencing primitive the HA coordinator issue needs — design the two together).
- Auth via the standard SDK default-credential chains; deps as optional extras (`sf2loki[s3]` → aioboto3 or aiobotocore; `sf2loki[gcs]` → gcloud-aio-storage) to keep the base image lean.
- Latency note: a per-flush ~20-50ms PUT serializes with the pipeline `_commit`; measure and, if needed, make commit fire-and-forget with a bounded pending window (careful: that weakens at-least-once to at-least-once-plus-slightly-more-duplicates on crash — document the trade or keep it synchronous).
- Tests against moto/fake-gcs-server style fakes; config validation for the new blocks; docs for Fargate/Cloud Run deployment (removes the volume section caveats).

## Acceptance criteria
- A Fargate task definition with no volume runs sf2loki durably; two instances against the same key fail fast rather than clobbering; checkpoint semantics (commit-after-push, duplicates-not-loss on crash) hold in integration tests.

comments.body: Scope decision (maintainer): this issue ships **S3 only** (the S3 API also covers MinIO/R2/Ceph via `endpoint_url`). Native GCS is split out to #37.

## Motivation
MSPs, ISV partners, and companies with several production orgs (plus sandboxes) currently need one sf2loki deployment per org — N containers, N configs, N state volumes for what is logically one job. Everything downstream already supports it: the `org` static label exists, streams separate cleanly, and checkpoints are namespaced by key.

## Proposal
Config becomes multi-org capable while staying backward compatible:
```yaml
orgs:
  - name: prod          # becomes the `org` label + checkpoint key prefix
    salesforce: {...}   # exactly today's salesforce block
    sources: {...}      # per-org source config
  - name: emea
    salesforce: {...}
    sources: {...}
sink: {...}             # shared
state: {...}            # shared store, keys prefixed org=<name>
service: {...}          # shared
```
Single-org configs (top-level `salesforce:`/`sources:`) keep working unchanged (internally normalized to a one-entry list).

## Implementation sketch
- `App.build` loops orgs: per-org `TokenProvider`, clients, sources, overlap guard, limits poller; ONE shared pipeline/sink/queue (backpressure and batching stay global; entries already carry labels). Checkpoint keys get an org prefix with a legacy-compat shim (unprefixed keys = first org) so existing state files migrate transparently.
- Config model: new `OrgConfig` wrapping today's `salesforce` + `sources`; a model validator enforcing exactly-one-of (top-level vs `orgs:` list) and unique org names; `just gen-config` regeneration.
- Metrics: add an `org` label to the per-source instruments (metrics.py touch — coordinate with dashboard regeneration; this is the largest mechanical part, list the affected instruments in the PR).
- Health/readiness: degraded-org reporting (one org's auth failing shouldn't kill the others — reuse the per-cycle containment patterns; startup fail-fast only if ALL orgs fail auth, WARN per failing org otherwise — this is a deliberate semantic change to today's fail-fast, call it out in docs).
- Sizing note in docs: API limits and Pub/Sub allocations are per org, so the existing guardrails apply per org automatically via per-org clients.

## Acceptance criteria
- Two orgs stream into one Loki tenant with distinct `org` labels from one container; single-org configs and existing state files work unchanged; one org's outage degrades (metrics + readiness reason) without stopping the other.

body:
## Motivation
Developers debugging Apex in real orgs rely on debug logs (`ApexLog`), which today live behind the Setup UI / Developer Console with 24h retention and manual download. Streaming them into Loki gives search, retention, and correlation with the RTEM/ELF events sf2loki already ships (REQUEST_ID appears in both worlds). This is a distinct persona (developer) from the current security/ops focus and a genuine differentiator for an OSS shipper.

## Proposal
An opt-in `sources.apexlog` polling source:
```yaml
sources:
  apexlog:
    enabled: false
    poll_interval: 1m
    users: ["integration@example.com"]   # only logs for these users (empty = all visible)
    max_body_bytes: 5242880              # skip larger bodies, keep the metadata row
```
Poll `SELECT Id, LogUserId, LogLength, Operation, Request, Status, StartTime, ... FROM ApexLog WHERE StartTime > :watermark` via the Tooling API, download bodies from `/tooling/sobjects/ApexLog/<id>/Body`, and ship each log either as one entry per log (body in the line, capped) or parsed per-line (follow-on). Labels: `source="apexlog"`, `event_type=Operation-ish`; user/request ids in structured metadata.

## Implementation sketch
- New `src/sf2loki/salesforce/apexlog_client.py` (Tooling API is the same REST auth/instance_url; reuse `SoqlClient` patterns with the `/tooling/query` path) + `src/sf2loki/sources/apexlog_source.py` reusing the eventlog_objects watermark/carry/error-containment patterns (StartTime watermark + Id dedup window; the >= + drain-until-short-page cursor already has a template).
- Body download = 1 API call per log — surface in docs and respect the throttle handling; `max_body_bytes` guard plus the existing line cap.
- IMPORTANT scoping honesty in docs: ApexLog only exists while a TraceFlag is active for a user; sf2loki should NOT manage TraceFlags in v1 (they expire by design, auto-renewal is a compliance decision) — document the `sf debug` / Setup steps to enable them, and consider `doctor` warning when apexlog is enabled but no active TraceFlags exist (`SELECT COUNT() FROM TraceFlag WHERE ExpirationDate > NOW`).
- Overlap guard: new category "apexlog", no collisions expected.
- Tests: respx fixtures for tooling query + body download; watermark/dedup replay tests mirroring eventlog_objects.

## Acceptance criteria
- With a TraceFlag active, Apex debug logs appear in Loki within one poll interval, checkpoint-resumable, size-capped, with API cost documented; disabled by default and absent from the free-tier quickstart path.

comments.body:
Implemented and shipped to `main` (commits `a9c0185..393faeb`), live-validated against a dev sandbox org.

**What shipped** (opt-in `sources.apexlog`, disabled by default):
- `SoqlClient` tooling-query mode; new `ApexLogClient` (Tooling API listing + one body download per log) and `ApexLogSource` (StartTime `>=` watermark + rolling Id-dedup window, checkpoint key `apexlog`).
- Raw debug-log body as the Loki line; metadata (`LogUserId`, `Operation`, `Status`, `Request`, `Application`, `DurationMilliseconds`, `Location`, `LogLength`, `Id`) + derived `level` in structured metadata. `event_type` is the fixed literal `apexlog` (Operation is a URL path — kept out of labels for cardinality).
- `users:` maps to a `LogUser.Username IN (...)` filter (verified live; usernames config-validated).
- `max_body_bytes` skips the body download (and its API call) for oversize logs, still shipping the metadata line flagged `body_skipped`.
- TraceFlags are **not** managed (they expire by design); `sf2loki doctor` adds a `traceflags` WARN when the source is enabled but no active TraceFlag exists.
- Metrics: `apexlog_logs_ingested`, `apexlog_download_bytes`, `apexlog_bodies_skipped`, `apexlog_download_errors`. Docs in README + DESIGN §8b + `docs/configuring-sources.md` §7.

Acceptance criteria met: logs appear in Loki within one poll interval, checkpoint-resumable, size-capped, API cost documented, disabled by default and absent from the free-tier quickstart.

body:
## Motivation
Salesforce's newer **Event Log Objects** store Event Monitoring data as queryable (big) objects with retention up to 1 year (paid option) — versus EventLogFile's 30-day CSV blobs with 3–6h landing latency. For orgs that have enabled them, ELO is a better ingestion backend for some types (row-level SOQL access, longer catch-up horizon after an outage, no CSV parsing) and the natural data source for the backfill command beyond ELF retention.

## Proposal
Investigate + implement `sources.eventlogfile.backend: files | objects` (or a distinct source) that reads the same event categories from their Event Log Object counterparts (e.g. `ApiEventLog`-style objects) via SOQL with an EventDate/timestamp watermark — reusing the eventlog_objects polling machinery (watermark + id-window + drain-until-short-page already exist) rather than the CSV path.

**Investigation first (timebox it):** the exact object names, which API surfaces expose them (SOQL vs Async SOQL vs Bulk), query cost/limits for big objects (big-object SOQL has restricted WHERE/ORDER semantics — the watermark cursor design must match what the index allows), licensing gates, and landing latency vs ELF. Write up findings in this issue before coding; the outcome may be "per-type allowlist only" or "not viable without Bulk API" — both are fine outcomes.

## Implementation sketch (assuming SOQL-queryable with an indexed timestamp)
- Generalize `EventLogObjectsSource` config to cover these objects (it already polls arbitrary objects by name + timestamp_field — possibly this is ONLY a preset + docs + overlap-category mapping exercise, which would be the ideal small outcome).
- Overlap guard: ELO-backed categories must map to the same category keys as their ELF/stream equivalents so double-ingest protection holds (extend `_CATEGORY_ALIASES`).
- Presets: `examples/presets/event-log-objects.yaml` for the common types; docs comparing the three backends (stream = seconds, ELO = minutes-hours?, ELF = 3-6h) once latency is measured.
- Backfill command integration: `--source objects` to reach beyond 30 days.

## Acceptance criteria
- Investigation findings documented in this issue (object names, query semantics, latency, licensing); if viable, at least the preset+alias path lands with tests, and the backfill command can read ELO history.

comments.body:
## Investigation findings (validated against a live org)

Probed the stored RTEM event objects directly (`LoginEvent`, `ApiEvent`, `FileEventStore`, `*EventStore`, ...):

- They are **Big Objects**. `ORDER BY <ts> ASC` → HTTP 400 `BIG_OBJECT_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` ("Unsupported order direction on filter column ... ASCENDING"). The timestamp index is **DESC-only**; `ORDER BY <ts> DESC` works.
- **No `nextRecordsUrl` pagination** — a full `LIMIT 200` page returns `done=true` with no cursor. Paging requires moving the `WHERE` bound.
- `COUNT()`/aggregates → `BIG_OBJECT_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION: Aggregate functions not supported`.
- `FIELDS(ALL)` itself works — only the ASC order was the blocker.
- Threat-detection anomaly stores (`ApiAnomalyEventStore` etc.) behave like standard objects (full audit fields, ASC works) — a different family.

So the "preset + alias only" outcome was **not** achievable: the ASC assumption was baked into the query builder. Shipped an engine branch instead.

## What shipped (commits `0678da5`→`be28a74`, gate green: 820 passed / 1 skipped)

Opt-in per-object **`big_object: true`** on `sources.eventlog_objects`. When set, the source drains newest-first (`ORDER BY <ts> DESC`) with a ratcheting `<=` upper bound, dedups within the drain **and** against the checkpoint id-window (cross-cycle), and re-sorts each cycle's window ascending before emitting through the shared `_emit_record` path — so the forward-only watermark, id-dedup, and crash-safety are identical to the ASC path. Also: an actionable log hint when an un-flagged object hits the ASC rejection, and `examples/presets/event-log-objects.yaml`.

## Backfill (`--source objects`) — descoped

Deliberately **not** building a dedicated ELO backfill. Loki rejects samples older than `reject_old_samples_max_age` (~1–2w), and the poll source's first-run `lookback` already reaches back as far as Loki will accept — a backfill command would mostly fetch data the sink then drops. The useful historical window is covered by `lookback`. If a genuine need for deeper history appears later (e.g. a longer Loki retention/`reject_old_samples_max_age`), it's a small follow-up on top of the `_drain_big_object` primitive.

Closing as complete.

body:
## Context
Issue #30 shipped remote checkpoint stores with **S3 only** (per maintainer scope decision — the S3 API also covers MinIO/R2/Ceph). This follow-up adds native Google Cloud Storage.

## Proposal
`state.store: gcs` implementing the `CheckpointStore` protocol, mirroring `src/sf2loki/state/s3_store.py`:
- Whole-document JSON at a configured bucket/object, in-memory cache, compare-and-swap commits via `ifGenerationMatch` (generation 0 for first write) — GCS's native precondition, the direct analogue of the S3 ETag If-Match used in s3_store.py. Precondition failure → the same split-brain fail-fast conflict error.
- `gcloud-aio-storage` as an optional extra (`sf2loki[gcs]`), lazily imported with the install-hint ConfigError from `state.build_store` (`src/sf2loki/state/__init__.py` — add the `gcs` case).
- Auth via Application Default Credentials.
- Same `set_fence` hook as the other stores.

## Acceptance criteria
A Cloud Run service with no volume runs sf2loki durably against GCS; two instances against one object fail fast; injected-fake-client unit tests mirror tests/state/test_s3_store.py; config + docs updated (`just gen-config`).

body:
The ASC drain pages with `WHERE {ts} >= {watermark} ORDER BY {ts} ASC LIMIT 200` and advances the watermark to each record's own timestamp (`src/sf2loki/sources/eventlog_objects_source.py:308-371`) — there is no secondary `Id` tiebreak in the ORDER BY or the WHERE. If ≥`_PAGE_LIMIT` (200) records share one timestamp `T` (bulk loads, API-event bursts, second-granularity timestamp fields), a full page consists entirely of records at `T`: the watermark can never rise above `T`, the next cycle re-issues the identical `>= T` query, and once the carried-id window has seen the page, `new_records` is empty on a full page — the loop warns "stopping this cycle to avoid a hot loop" and breaks (`:356-366`). That warning is actually a **permanent stall**: every cycle repeats it, records at `T` beyond the first page are never fetched, and everything newer than `T` is silently never ingested. The big-object DESC drain has the symmetric defect (`new_in_page == 0` guard, `:499-508`). `_MAX_CARRIED_IDS` governs eviction, not progress.

Impact: permanent, silent, total ingestion halt for the affected object; `sf2loki_watermark_ts` staleness is the only external signal.

Resolution steps:
1. Add a secondary cursor for the ASC path: `ORDER BY {ts} ASC, Id ASC` with `WHERE ({ts} > :wm) OR ({ts} = :wm AND Id > :last_id)` so a full page of ties still advances.
2. Give `_drain_big_object` the equivalent escape (Big Object index constraints may rule out a compound ORDER BY — if so, make the id-window page-aware instead of breaking the drain).
3. Escalate the `:358` warning to ERROR + a dedicated metric when the same boundary repeats across cycles, so any residual stall is alertable.
4. Regression tests: >`_PAGE_LIMIT` records at one timestamp drain completely on both paths.

Same missing-tiebreak pattern as #38, in the ApexLog source: the listing is `ORDER BY StartTime ASC LIMIT 200` (`src/sf2loki/salesforce/apexlog_client.py:109`) with no `Id` tiebreak, and the watermark advances to `StartTime` (`src/sf2loki/sources/apexlog_source.py`). >200 ApexLog rows at one StartTime (parallel batch/async Apex is the realistic trigger) fill the page with one timestamp, the carried-id window dedups it, and the watermark never advances — newer debug logs are silently dropped forever.

Impact: smaller blast radius than #38 (opt-in source, developer-debugging data), but the same silent permanent stall.

Resolution steps:
1. `(StartTime, Id)` compound cursor, as in #38.
2. Shared regression test covering the full-page-tie case for this source.

body:
`backfill.py:552` keys progress as `backfill:{interval}:{event_type}` with no org component, and the backfill state file derives from the shared `cfg.state.file.path` (`backfill.py:704-706`); `as_single_org_view` copies only `salesforce`/`sources` and leaves `state` shared. Running `backfill --org A ...` then `backfill --org B ...` for the same interval/event-type makes B load A's `last_created` watermark and skip every org-B file older than it — silently, with no warning. (The live daemon is unaffected: its keys carry the `org=<name>:` prefix via `state/org_view.py`.)

Impact: multi-org customers doing per-org backfills silently lose history for every org after the first.

Resolution steps:
1. Include the org in the backfill checkpoint key (`backfill:org={name}:{interval}:{event_type}`), with a legacy-key fallback for the first configured org mirroring `state/org_view.py`.
2. Test: two-org config, backfill org A then org B over the same window — B must list from its own watermark.

body:
`csv.field_size_limit()` is never raised anywhere in src/, so the stdlib 128 KiB per-field cap applies; ELF free-text columns (QUERY / URI / USER_AGENT / stack traces) can exceed it, making `csv.Error` deterministic for that file (`src/sf2loki/salesforce/eventlogfile_client.py:244-248`). The first-row failure path has the `download_max_age` abandon escape (`src/sf2loki/sources/eventlogfile_source.py:572-599`), but the mid-file path (`:627-635`) always returns without abandoning — and the failing file is the watermark boundary, so it is re-downloaded and re-failed every cycle, wedging the whole EventType forever.

Impact: permanent silent stall of an entire EventType on one oversized field; watermark staleness is the only signal. A row-1 fault self-heals, the identical fault on row 2+ never does — inconsistent by accident.

Resolution steps:
1. Raise `csv.field_size_limit` to at least `batch.max_line_bytes` (oversized lines are already capped downstream by the sink).
2. Give the mid-file failure path the same `download_max_age` abandon escape as the first-row path.
3. Test: a file with an oversized field mid-file eventually abandons and the type keeps progressing.

body:
`_event_timestamp` (`src/sf2loki/sources/pubsub_source.py:588-590`) calls `extract_timestamp(...)` with no `fallback=` and not the `_checked` variant, so an event carrying none of `EventDate`/`CreatedDate`/`commitTimestamp` (custom platform events and CDC channels are the realistic case) gets `datetime.now(UTC)` from `shaping.py:233-234`. Replayed deliveries of the same event then get a different timestamp each time, so Loki stores duplicates instead of collapsing byte-identical entries — and because the unchecked variant is used, no `timestamp_fallbacks` metric fires, so it is invisible.

This is the same bug class #20 fixed for the polling sources; the pubsub path was missed.

Resolution steps:
1. Use `extract_timestamp_checked` with a stable per-event fallback (clamped like the #20 fix), so replays are deterministic.
2. Count fallbacks in the existing `timestamp_fallbacks` metric.
3. Test: an event with no parsable time fields produces the same timestamp on redelivery.

body:
Three related visibility/boundedness gaps around Pub/Sub decode and schema failures:

1. A payload that fails Avro decode is skipped and the checkpoint advances past it with the next good event (`src/sf2loki/salesforce/pubsub_client.py:316-319`). That drop-and-advance is the accepted at-least-once tradeoff — but `decode_errors` has **no topic label**, so you cannot tell which topic is losing events, and no shipped alert fires on it.
2. If **every** event on a topic fails decode (systemic schema/codec incompatibility), the stream makes zero progress silently: nothing is yielded, `received` never flips (`pubsub_source.py:420`), `pubsub_stream_up` stays 0 but the 300s stall watchdog never fires because responses ARE arriving — the server redelivers from the stale cursor forever and every event is dropped on every pass.
3. A permanently unfetchable schema (`SchemaFetchError` re-raise → reconnect → replay) is correct for the transient case but indistinguishable from healthy reconnect churn when permanent — the topic replays the same replay_id forever with only `pubsub_reconnects` climbing.

Resolution steps:
1. Add a `topic` label to `decode_errors` and ship an alert on it (silent-data-loss tier in `deploy/grafana/gen_alerts.py`).
2. Treat N consecutive batches with 100% decode failure, or M consecutive schema-fetch failures on one topic, as a distinct stalled state: dedicated metric + ERROR log, alertable.

body:
`Pipeline._commit` → `store.commit()` has no retry (`src/sf2loki/app.py:401-408`), and neither the S3 store (`s3_store.py:174-207`) nor the GCS store (`gcs_store.py:146-178`) retries anything — they only classify the CAS precondition failure. A routine transient object-store error on the checkpoint PUT (`503 SlowDown`, `InternalError`, TCP reset — normal under throttling) propagates out of the consumer task, `Pipeline.run` re-raises, and `_on_pipeline_done` crashes the whole process (`app.py:1004-1013`). Every other external call in the codebase (auth, Loki, SOQL, ELF download, limits) retries transient errors in-process; only the checkpoint store doesn't. `EgressGovernor.record` (`egress.py:258`) shares the surface.

Impact: under sustained S3/GCS throttling the daemon crash-loops, dropping every gRPC stream and re-authing all orgs on each iteration — turning a transient store hiccup into org-wide ingestion churn.

Resolution steps:
1. Bounded, jittered retry (tenacity, mirroring the sink's discipline) around transient errors inside the S3/GCS `commit`/`load` paths.
2. Keep the precondition-conflict (fencing/split-brain) classification fail-fast and immediate — that one MUST still crash.
3. Test: a store stub that 503s twice then succeeds → pipeline survives without restart; a 412 still raises `StateStoreConflictError`.

body:
`_run_topic` loads its replay position — `stored = await state.load(f"pubsub:{topic}")` at `src/sf2loki/sources/pubsub_source.py:387` — BEFORE the try/finally that guarantees the queue sentinel (`try:` at `:404`, sentinel in its finally). If that load raises (transient S3/GCS error at leadership acquisition), or `base64.b64decode(stored)` at `:389` raises on a corrupt checkpoint value, the topic task dies **without its sentinel**. `events()`'s drain loop (`:288-289`) then waits forever; `_drain_with_grace` force-cancels after `shutdown_grace` and returns cleanly; `_on_pipeline_done` sees a clean completion with `run_stop` unset → `stop.set()` → the process exits **0**. Under docker `restart: on-failure` the daemon stays dead with a success exit code.

Resolution steps:
1. Move the checkpoint load (and the b64 decode, falling back to `replay_preset` on a corrupt value with an ERROR + metric) inside the reconnect loop's try, so a failure backs off and retries like any other stream error.
2. Regression test: a `state.load` that raises once must not wedge `events()` or exit 0.

body:
`_drain_big_object` (`src/sf2loki/sources/eventlog_objects_source.py:444-526`) accumulates the entire cycle window into a `collected` dict and only emits after the drain completes (needed to re-sort the DESC pages ascending) — so the #16 pipeline byte bound never applies during collection. Steady state is one poll interval of data, but a first-run lookback or a post-outage catch-up (watermark correctly held back during a long Loki outage) drains the whole gap into memory, unbounded by any config. The docstring acknowledges the buffering.

Impact: exactly the recovery moment after an outage — when the service is finally healthy again — is when a high-volume Big Object can OOM it.

Resolution steps:
1. Cap the per-cycle window (max records and/or max window duration), ratcheting the bound across cycles so catch-up proceeds in bounded chunks rather than one giant drain.
2. Or emit per ratchet segment instead of per full drain (each segment is internally sorted; the watermark/dedup semantics already tolerate cross-cycle boundaries).
3. Test: a synthetic multi-page catch-up stays under the configured cap.

body:
`check_fence()` reads only the local `self._is_leader` boolean (`src/sf2loki/coordinate/file_lease.py:99-110`, `k8s_lease.py:150-161`), which flips only when `_hold`'s next re-read notices a foreign holder — up to a `renew_interval` late, or arbitrarily late across an event-loop stall. The commit path is fence-check → await I/O → write (TOCTOU), and the **file** store's `_flush` is a blind tmp+rename with no compare-and-swap (`state/file_store.py:125-145`). So a deposed-but-unaware leader passes the fence and can overwrite keys the new leader already advanced — checkpoint regression, i.e. a re-ingest window beyond the documented one-ttl bound. The S3/GCS stores incidentally catch this via their own ETag/generation CAS; the shared-file deployment — the primary file-lease HA topology — has no backstop. README's "a stale leader … is refused at commit time and cannot race the new leader's checkpoints" overstates what the boolean fence guarantees.

Impact: no data loss (commit still strictly follows push), but duplicates beyond the documented bound, and a fencing guarantee in the docs that the file store doesn't actually provide.

Resolution steps:
1. Make the fence a real token: write holder/epoch into the lease, thread it through commits, and verify it atomically at write time (file store: re-read the lease holder under the same rename discipline, or embed the epoch in the state doc and verify+swap).
2. At minimum, correct the README fencing claim for the file-store topology.
3. Test: a fenced-out stale leader's commit is rejected even when its local boolean still says leader.

body:
All three checkpoint stores cache the state document for process lifetime — `_ensure_loaded` short-circuits once `_cache is not None` (`file_store.py:103`, `s3_store.py:147`, `gcs_store.py:119`) — and nothing resets it on leadership loss: `on_lose` (`app.py:1034-1038`) tears down the pipeline only. But the coordinator explicitly supports acquire → lose → re-acquire cycles on one process.

On re-acquisition after another instance led in between: sources `load()` stale checkpoints → re-ingest everything the other leader advanced past (duplicates); the file store's next commit can regress the shared file (compounding #47); the S3/GCS stores hit a CAS conflict on their first commit → `StateStoreConflictError` → process crash, recovering only via restart-and-reload.

Resolution steps:
1. Add a `reset()`/invalidate hook to the stores (duck-typed, like `set_fence`) clearing `_cache` + etag/generation, and wire it into `on_lose`.
2. Test: demote → (external state change) → promote serves fresh values and commits cleanly.

body:
The file store's exclusive-instance flock on the `.lock` sidecar is taken on first use and released only in `close()` at process exit (`src/sf2loki/state/file_store.py:81-98, 62-70`) — never on demotion. In a file-lease HA pair sharing the state volume (the documented topology), the demoted-but-alive old leader still holds the flock when the promoted standby's first commit tries to acquire it:

- Where flock propagates cross-host (working NFS lockd, EFS): the NEW leader gets `StateFileLockError`, which is not absorbed (only `StateFenceError` is, `app.py:1066-1069`) → crash → restart → still locked → **crash-loop with no active leader until the old process dies**.
- Where it doesn't propagate (NFS `local_lock` — the exact unreliability `file_lease.py:10-13` cites for rejecting flock in the lease): the flock is a silent no-op and provides no protection at all.

Either way the mechanism doesn't fit the HA topology it ships alongside.

Resolution steps:
1. Release the flock on demotion (close/reopen the store per acquisition — pairs naturally with the cache-invalidation hook in the demote/promote issue), or
2. Skip the sidecar flock when a real coordinator is configured (the lease IS the exclusivity mechanism) and document the NFS caveat for standalone deployments.
3. Test: file-lease failover on a shared tmpdir — promoted store commits without crashing while the old process is still alive.

body:
`_read` maps ANY `OSError` (not just `FileNotFoundError`) to `None`/"absent" (`src/sf2loki/coordinate/file_lease.py:246-254`). Two consequences:

1. In `_hold`, a `None` re-read skips the foreign-holder surrender branch (`:197-198`) and the leader blindly re-writes the lease with no verify, staying leader; concurrently a standby's `_acquire` also sees `None`, writes, verify-reads itself, and declares leadership → **two active leaders** for up to a `renew_interval`. Trigger: lease-file deletion (operator cleanup). The k8s backend got exactly this fixed in bb00032 (404-on-renew → surrender); the file backend has no equivalent, so `rm leader.lease` is worse on the file backend than on k8s.
2. A transient NFS read error on a standby is indistinguishable from "absent", so it contests a lease a live leader still holds; if its rename lands last, false takeover.

Resolution steps:
1. In `_hold`, treat a missing/unreadable lease as contested: go through the pause + verify-read path (as `_acquire` does) instead of a blind rewrite — surrender if the verify shows a foreign holder.
2. In `_acquire`, distinguish `FileNotFoundError` (claimable) from other `OSError`s (back off and re-poll) before contesting.
3. Tests: delete-the-lease-mid-hold converges to exactly one leader within a renew interval; a read error does not trigger takeover.

body:
Lease expiry is `renew_time + duration >= observer's utcnow()` (`src/sf2loki/coordinate/k8s_lease.py:56-57`), where `renewTime` was written from the LEADER's wall clock (`:238-244, 313-320`) and read back verbatim (`:461-469`) — a cross-host wall-clock comparison. A standby whose clock runs ahead of the leader's by more than the safety margin sees a live lease as expired and takes over prematurely → split-brain window (duplicates, plus the fence/cache races of #47/#48). client-go's leaderelection deliberately does NOT trust `renewTime` for this exact reason: it records an `observedTime` on the observer's own clock whenever the lease content changes, and measures staleness against that.

The README HA section currently claims "no NTP concern beyond the API server's own clock" — wrong as implemented; today the k8s backend has the same inter-host skew sensitivity as the file lease, just undocumented.

Resolution steps:
1. Adopt the observedTime pattern: track (locally, monotonic) when the lease's `renewTime`/`resourceVersion` was last seen to change; expire relative to that, ignoring the leader's clock.
2. Fix the README claim either way.
3. Test: a lease renewed by a "slow-clock" leader is not considered expired by a "fast-clock" observer within lease_duration of observed change.

body:
`App.build` wraps the duck-typed store close as a sync call (`src/sf2loki/app.py:911-917`):

```python
state_close = getattr(state, "close", None)
if callable(state_close):
    async def _close_state() -> None:
        state_close()
```

`FileCheckpointStore.close()` is sync so the file backend is fine — but `S3CheckpointStore.close()` (`s3_store.py:209`) and `GcsCheckpointStore.close()` (`gcs_store.py:180`) are `async def`. The call constructs a coroutine and discards it: the aiobotocore/gcloud-aio client session is never closed (`RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'close' was never awaited`), leaking the connector on every graceful shutdown — one per restart/failover cycle. `getattr` types the callable `Any`, which is exactly why `mypy --strict` can't see the missing await.

Resolution steps:
1. Branch on `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(state_close)` and await it — or make `close()` uniformly async across all three stores and always await.
2. Add the missing composition-root test: `App.build()` with an s3/gcs state config, run shutdown, assert the store's close actually executed (the per-store unit tests can't catch this wiring bug).

body:
## Motivation

Every source of every org fans into ONE bounded queue drained by ONE consumer that awaits each Loki push serially (`src/sf2loki/app.py:189-191`, `:356-399`). Process-wide throughput ceiling ≈ `max_entries / (encode + push RTT)` — with the 1000-entry default and ~100 ms Grafana Cloud RTT, roughly 10k entries/s **total**. When a big org's Daily ELF cycle lands tens of millions of rows, draining takes tens of minutes; the whole time the shared queue is full, so every other producer blocks — including other orgs' realtime Pub/Sub streams (flow-control credits stop being topped up, Salesforce stops sending). One queue = shared fate: a batch workload starves the latency-sensitive one. #16 bounded the memory and #25 parallelized the ELF fetch, but neither touches the single-lane drain.

## Proposal

Separate ingestion classes so bulk cannot starve streaming:
- at minimum two lanes (streaming vs bulk/ELF), each its own queue + push worker; optionally per-org lanes with fair scheduling;
- bounded concurrent Loki pushes (2–4 in flight) — per-key commit ordering only requires per-source FIFO, which per-class lanes preserve (checkpoint keys are disjoint across sources).

## Implementation sketch

`Pipeline` grows a small set of (queue, consumer) lanes keyed by source class; `_flush`/`_commit` stay per-lane so the commit-after-push invariant is untouched. Config: automatic classification (pubsub → streaming; eventlogfile/eventlog_objects/apexlog → bulk) with the single-lane behavior available for compatibility. Reuse the existing byte-budget accounting per lane.

## Acceptance criteria

- An integration test with a saturated bulk lane shows pubsub ingest lag bounded by ~one flush interval (today it grows with the ELF backlog).
- Commit-after-push and per-key monotonicity preserved (existing pipeline tests still green).
- README/DESIGN updated for the lane model.

comments.body:
**Deferred from the #38–#72 prod-readiness wave** to its own session (deliberate — this rearchitects the safety-critical commit-after-push pipeline and warrants a design-doc-first, high-accuracy pass). Everything else in that wave is on `main`.

**Design worked out during the deferral** (validate, then refine):
- Split sources into lane **classes**: streaming (pubsub) vs bulk (eventlogfile / eventlog_objects / apexlog). Each lane gets its own `asyncio.Queue` + consumer + `_flush`/`_commit` + **byte budget**. Per-key FIFO (and per-key commit monotonicity) is preserved because each source's checkpoint keys are disjoint and stay within one lane. Two lanes ⇒ up to 2 concurrent Loki pushes, satisfying the "2–4 in flight" ask with no extra machinery.
- **Per-lane byte budget is mandatory, not optional.** A shared budget would let a bulk drain saturate it and block pubsub via `_charge` — the exact starvation this issue fixes. That's what makes the change invasive: `_charge`/`_release`/`_produce`/`_consume` must key off a lane-state object, not the pipeline-global `self._queued_bytes`/`self._byte_cond`.
- **Single-lane default:** when all sources classify to one lane (e.g. the all-`"test"`-named fakes in `test_pipeline.py`), behaviour must stay byte-identical so existing tests pass.
- Introduce an internal `_LaneState` (queue, byte_cond, queued_bytes, name); build lanes inside `run()`; generalise the FIRST_EXCEPTION crash/drain orchestration across N (queue, consumer) pairs — a consumer finishing is now normal (one lane drained); a consumer finishing *with an exception* is the crash signal.

**Known couplings / risks to handle:**
- ~6 tests call pipeline internals directly and will need updating: `test_pipeline.py` `pipe._produce(src, queue, …)` (byte-budget + queue-depth tests) and `pipe._release(item)`. Keep the `pipe._queue_maxsize` attribute (read by `test_pipeline` + `test_app_integration`).
- `sf2loki_queue_depth` is unlabelled and set to `queue.qsize()`; with N lanes decide sum-vs-per-lane (a single-lane test asserts `== 3.0`).
- `EgressGovernor` is shared across lanes and **should** stay global (deployment-wide budget) — but concurrent `admit()`/`record()` from two consumers can interleave its token bucket between awaits; assess and either accept+document or guard without serialising lanes.
- Worst-case buffered memory becomes ~`n_lanes × queue_max_bytes` if each lane gets the full budget — decide (full-per-lane + documented, or split) and update the #56 memory math.
- README/DESIGN need the lane model documented (acceptance criterion).

**Process:** design doc → adversarial self-review (attack commit-after-push, crash orchestration, governor race, memory bound) → TDD. Acceptance test: a saturated bulk lane (flooding source + slow sink) shows pubsub ingest lag bounded by ~one flush interval while the bulk backlog drains. Keep all existing pipeline tests green.

body:
`Pipeline._commit` loops the batch's distinct keys and calls `store.commit(key, value)` once per key (`src/sf2loki/app.py:401-408`). Every file-store commit re-serializes the WHOLE cache and fsyncs both the file and its parent dir (`state/file_store.py:125-145`); every s3/gcs commit re-uploads the full JSON document per key (`s3_store.py:174-207`, `gcs_store.py:146-178`). The document is not small: ELF checkpoint values embed up-to-200-pair carried-id windows (~10 KB each), so multi-org wildcard deployments carry a multi-MB state doc.

Consequences at load:
- file store: a multi-key flush at a high flush rate = event-loop-blocking fsync storms (2 fsyncs × keys × flush rate) — the fsyncs are synchronous on the loop, stalling every producer;
- s3/gcs: N keys per flush = N serial full-object conditional PUTs inside the flush path (latency ceiling + PUT cost). The README's "one GET+PUT per checkpoint flush" is really per-key-per-flush.

Resolution steps:
1. Add a multi-key `commit_many(dict)` to the stores; `_commit` calls it once per flush (one serialize + one write).
2. Run file-store writes/fsyncs via `asyncio.to_thread`.
3. Optionally coalesce s3/gcs commits on a short interval — checkpoint lag ≤ one interval is already within the at-least-once contract.

body:
Two coverage gaps in the #16 queue byte budget:

1. **Per-source bridge queues aren't byte-bounded.** `PubSubSource.events()` bridges its topic tasks through an internal `asyncio.Queue(maxsize=queue_maxsize)` (default 1000 entries, `src/sf2loki/sources/pubsub_source.py:264`) UPSTREAM of the pipeline's byte accounting. During a sink outage that's up to `queue_maxsize x max_line_bytes` (~256 MB worst case) of additional buffering per org that the #16 budget never sees.
2. **Entry cost undercounts real memory.** `_entry_cost` counts only `len(line) + 64` (`src/sf2loki/app.py:237-247`), ignoring the labels dict, structured_metadata dict, and the checkpoint value string. ELF entries each carry a ~10 KB carried-id-window checkpoint string (see #69 — re-serialized per row today), so real RAM at the configured bound can be ~1.5-2x the budget — precisely during the sink outage the bound exists for.

Resolution steps:
1. Byte-bound the pubsub bridge queue with the same charge/release pattern (or size it in bytes).
2. Include approximate checkpoint/label/metadata sizes in `_entry_cost` (cheap approximations fine) and document the revised worst-case memory math.

`docker-compose.yml` sets no `stop_grace_period`, so Docker SIGKILLs 10s (its default) after SIGTERM — while the app budgets a 25s drain (`service.shutdown_grace`, `src/sf2loki/config.py:1241-1244`) plus a separate 5s closer budget (`app.py:_CLOSE_TIMEOUT`). 2. Document ECS `stopTimeout` in the README's ECS paragraph and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` in the k8s example (#60).

body:
## Motivation

There is no supported way to inspect or repair checkpoints. On the file store an operator can hand-edit JSON (undocumented, risky, and racing the flock); on s3/gcs there is nothing. When a watermark wedges (the failure family in #38/#39/#41), the alert runbooks in docs/alerts.md stop at "check logs/permissions" — none explains how to *advance past* a poison record, or what the duplicate-window consequences of doing so are.

## Proposal

```
sf2loki state show   [--key GLOB] --config config.yaml   # pretty-print checkpoints from the CONFIGURED store
sf2loki state set    KEY VALUE --config config.yaml      # CAS-safe write
sf2loki state delete KEY --config config.yaml            # remove a key (source restarts from preset/lookback)
```

Operating through `build_store(cfg.state)` so file/s3/gcs all work, honouring the CAS and refusing (without `--force`) when the daemon holds the file-store flock.

## Implementation sketch

New `state` subcommand in `cli.py` beside doctor/backfill; reuse the store factory; redact nothing (checkpoint values aren't secret). A `docs/` runbook section: how to identify the stuck key from `watermark_ts`, what deleting vs setting it does, and the resulting duplicate window.

## Acceptance criteria

- Works against all three stores; s3/gcs conflict-safe.
- Refuses a locked file store unless `--force`.
- Runbook section linked from docs/alerts.md's WatermarkStale/PushesStalled entries.

The polling sources advance their in-memory cursor when rows are dropped by transforms or sampled out, but never emit `checkpoint_only` tokens (`src/sf2loki/sources/eventlog_objects_source.py:411-419`, `eventlogfile_source.py:680-689`, `apexlog_source.py:187-196`) — a cycle whose entries are ALL filtered emits nothing, so nothing durable advances. The next cycle (and every cycle after a restart) re-fetches and deterministically re-drops the same window.

Impact: churn, not loss — wasted SOQL/download API budget and re-transform CPU, invisible downstream because the drops are deterministic. Worst for a heavily-sampled high-volume object or an aggressive drop_row transform.

Resolution steps:
1. Yield a `checkpoint_only` token at cycle end when the cursor advanced but nothing was emitted — the pubsub source already has exactly this pattern for keepalive replay_ids, and the pipeline commits such tokens through the same FIFO path.
2. Test: a fully-sampled-out cycle advances the stored watermark.

body:
`_is_invalid_argument` keys only on the gRPC status code (`src/sf2loki/sources/pubsub_source.py:517-519`), so ANY `INVALID_ARGUMENT` while resuming a CUSTOM replay — not just a genuinely corrupted/expired replay id — is treated as corrupt and triggers the fallback re-subscribe from EARLIEST. A malformed subscribe argument (e.g. after a client library upgrade or a Salesforce API change) would silently re-drain the topic's full retention window: bounded duplicates, no loss, but a large re-ingest bill on a high-volume topic, misattributed to replay corruption.

Salesforce attaches an error-info trailer (`...replayid.corrupted` family) identifying the real case.

Resolution steps:
1. Inspect the error trailer and only take the EARLIEST fallback when it confirms replay-id corruption/expiry; other INVALID_ARGUMENTs follow the normal backoff-and-retry path (they'll surface as a reconnect loop → visible, not a silent re-drain).
2. Keep the code-only heuristic as a fallback when no trailer is present; keep the `pubsub_replay_fallbacks` metric either way.

`settle_window` defaults to 0 while `interval` defaults to `Hourly` (`src/sf2loki/config.py:643,686`). Hourly EventLogFile blobs are not regenerated in place — if a blob is listed and ingested while server-side incomplete, and the watermark then passes it, any missing tail rows are permanently skipped. Network-level truncation IS handled (content-length verification, watermark safety on transient failure); a blob Salesforce itself finalized late is not. Severity is SUSPECTED (depends on Salesforce's write-then-list visibility semantics, which aren't documented), but the guard already exists and defaulting it on is cheap insurance.

Resolution steps:
1. Default `settle_window` to a conservative non-zero value (5-10m) when `interval: Hourly`; Daily can stay 0 (files land long after the day closes).
2. Release-note the changed default (ingestion latency for Hourly types grows by the window).

body:
Two multi-org (#31) wiring rough edges:

1. **Per-org ELF clock-skew hooks stack on the shared httpx client.** Every org's `EventLogFileClient` appends its `_capture_server_date` response hook to the ONE shared `sf_http` client (`src/sf2loki/salesforce/eventlogfile_client.py:109-111`; the client is shared across all orgs, `app.py:779`). With N orgs, N hooks fire on EVERY Salesforce response for ANY org — and each org's `_clock_skew` gets overwritten by whatever org's response fired last. The skew feeds the ELF settle/abandon gates, so org A's gate can run on org B's server clock (different SF instances can differ). Plus O(orgs) hook overhead per response.
2. **Startup auth probe is sequential.** `_probe_orgs` awaits each org's token one at a time (`app.py:1081-1088`) — 10 orgs at ~300 ms each is multi-second serial startup before readiness, trivially `asyncio.gather`-able (the some-fail degraded semantics are per-org already).

Resolution steps:
1. Capture the Date header per-request inside the ELF client's own calls (or filter the shared hook by the org's instance host) so each org sees only its own skew.
2. `asyncio.gather` the startup probe, preserving the all-fail/some-fail semantics.

Individually small costs multiplied by event rate, worth one pass with a saturated-pipeline benchmark:

1. **Per-row checkpoint re-serialization**: ELF and eventlog_objects rebuild the (identical for every non-final row) checkpoint value with `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` over an up-to-200-pair id window for EVERY emitted row (`src/sf2loki/sources/eventlogfile_source.py:710-716`, `eventlog_objects_source.py:431-433`). Hoist to once per file/page and reuse the string.
2. **Triple UTF-8 encode per entry**: the line is encoded for the producer byte-charge (`app.py:247`), again in `_consume`'s batch accounting (`:315`), and again for the governor (`:342`). Compute once, thread through.
3. **Per-event `datetime.now(UTC)`** + fresh labels-dict merge in `_produce` (`app.py:220-226`); multi-org adds a second dict rebuild + CheckpointToken alloc per entry (`sources/org_adapter.py:114-117`).
4. `route_fields` does `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)` per event (`shaping.py:54`) and `cap_line` a full re-encode per line (`shaping.py:161`) — candidates for the same single-encode pass.

(Related but separate: fastavro decode runs on-loop per event, `salesforce/avro_codec.py:63` — C-fast, only worth offloading if profiling shows it.)

## Summary
Ship a comprehensive, production-ready Helm chart at `deploy/helm/` and publish it as an OCI chart to `ghcr.io/rknightion/charts/sf2loki`, so Kubernetes deployment is a single install/upgrade path instead of hand-applied manifests.

## Scope
- Full chart: Deployment (uid/gid 10001, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, drop ALL caps, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`), ConfigMap, ServiceAccount, optional Service + PodDisruptionBudget.
- **Single-instance-by-default guard:** `replicaCount>1` without `ha.enabled` fails the render (the Pub/Sub API has no consumer groups, so extra replicas would double-ingest).
- **Active-passive HA** (`ha.enabled`): lease RBAC (`Role`/`RoleBinding` scoped to the one Lease, never cluster-wide) + host/zone anti-affinity/spread.
- Secrets as mounted files: create-from-values / `existingSecret` / External Secrets Operator (AWS/GCP).
- Opt-in NetworkPolicy: Salesforce / Pub/Sub (`:7443`) / Loki / OTLP / state / API-server egress, with Cilium `toFQDNs` notes (plain NetworkPolicy can't match FQDNs).
- **Publishing** rides the shared `container-publish.yml` reusable via `helm-chart-path: deploy/helm` (cosign-signed, attached to each release); release-please bumps `deploy/helm/Chart.yaml`.

Part of the fleet-wide docs effort tracked in **rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28** (Phase 2). This repo's doc site is served under the m7kni.io hub at `/sf2loki/`, so its own Zensical build + theme overrides determine what search engines and LLMs see for these pages.

Two things are bundled here because they touch the same files:

1. **Redesign & rebrand alignment** — adopt the new m7kni.io brand and colour scheme (light-first, the shared wordmark / palette / type tokens) so the whole fleet reads as one product family. **Tune it for documentation, not marketing:** unlike the vibrant hub *landing* page, these are end-user **product documentation** sites — prioritise a clean, professional, highly readable, documentation-friendly presentation (sensible density, strong nav/TOC/search, scannable reference content) while staying on-brand in palette, type, and logo. Brand-consistent, docs-first. The exact spec follows from the hub redesign — treat the visual details as **pending finalization in rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28** and don't front-run them.
2. **SEO / LLM discoverability** — the metadata improvements below, fully specified now and able to proceed independently of the visual spec.

## Why (SEO/LLM part)

Like the hub, this site's `docs/overrides/main.html` is an empty passthrough, so OpenGraph/Twitter/JSON-LD/robots meta are either absent or (if copied from the hub) injected client-side and invisible to non-JS crawlers and LLMs (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot, social unfurlers). Render them server-side.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Redesign & rebrand alignment** — apply the finalized hub brand/scheme in a professional, documentation-friendly way (spec via rknightion/m7kni-net-site#28). Brand-consistent palette/type/logo; docs-first layout, density, and navigation.
- [ ] **Server-render head tags** — `main.html` `extrahead` override emitting canonical, `theme-color`, OpenGraph, Twitter (`summary_large_image`), and `robots` meta server-side, reading `config.extra.*` + `page.meta.*`. Mirror the hub's implementation once #29 lands (reuse the same override pattern). ⚠️ MiniJinja — no Python string methods.
- [ ] **JSON-LD** — per-page `Article` (not `TechArticle`) + a repo-level `SoftwareSourceCode`/`SoftwareApplication` node (name, description, `programmingLanguage`, `codeRepository` → this GitHub repo). `Organization` site-wide.
- [ ] **Remove any client-side `seo.js`** if this repo carries a copy; server-side supersedes it.
- [ ] **GEO content-shape pass** on the docs prose (biggest evidence-backed LLM-citation win): definition-first sentences (lead a config option with what it does), self-contained/chunkable `##`/`###` sections (restate the subject, don't rely on "it"/"this"), config/flag/env reference as **tables** not prose, language-tagged code fences (```yaml/```bash), strict one-H1-per-page hierarchy.
- [ ] **robots.txt** — ensure this repo's `docs/robots.txt` allows the current AI UAs (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent`, plus user-action bots). (Note: the hub regenerates per-site `robots.txt` at merge time — keep the source consistent with the hub's policy.)
